changes: Device center delegates computer information to the existing registered open_computer_adaptation action and kernel surface. Its private Tauri query, browser session vault, unlocked/connected labels and related state are deleted.
Eighteen unused translation entries belonging to the removed device panel are deleted. Device discovery, pairing, sensors and remote endpoints are unchanged.

All seven ApiKeyField call sites already save server credentials. The unused browser persistence, optional server-key branch, secret/text switch and unused compact prop are deleted; the existing cleanup of legacy browser keys remains.

Credential save and removal share one handler and return the verified server status. Existing useModelOperation owns saving, probing, error output, cancellation and deadlines instead of separate saved/testing/test-result state and success timers.

Account, role and server-key identity remount the credential editor. Initial status failures block editing and allow explicit retry; failed save verification preserves drafts; unsaved drafts disable probing so tests use confirmed credentials.

Probe messages remain visible inline and preserve recognition/synthesis failure details. Save/remove keep success and failure toasts; the separate two-second checkmark and duplicate probe toasts are removed.
validationNotes: Nine new parameterized cases cover device navigation on browser, Electron and Tauri host markers; a real credential-service POST/GET save/removal sequence; serialization; legacy-key cleanup; read retry; retained failed drafts; speech-probe errors/retry; and late read/save/probe results after account changes.
Device navigation tests render the actual DeviceSyncCenter, observe its event and resolve the actual surface registry. They do not mount the whole desktop shell or exercise a native window.

Credential tests execute production ApiKeyField, ServerApiKeyField, ModelSettingsStatus and useModelOperation with real settingsKeys/apiClient over synthetic fetch. Disclosure chrome, button styling and icons are test substitutes.

The existing related suites cover registered client surfaces, render-commit requirements, computer exploration consent and lifecycle, model settings behavior and real host system-stat sampling. Final source fingerprints match test/build receipts and preserve prune40-63 baselines.
limitations: This deletes the misleading duplicate system panel; it does not change SystemService fallbacks, kernel telemetry error handling or native bridges. The kernel monitor still has its existing behavior and limits.
Credentials remain in the existing machine-wide backend store. UI cancellation cannot undo a backend-accepted write and does not provide cross-client transactions.
LLMProviderRow and RelayProviderRow still contain separate credential state/write handlers. They were inspected but not merged in this batch.
Business source decreases by 119 lines, tests grow by 86, and total source decreases by 33. No new production/test file or business subsystem was created.
No real credentials, external provider call, full-suite run, native-client acceptance, backend rebuild, user-data change, commit, push or client restart.
